findings.issue_text: [BUG] The zero-length override check compares two Dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality of distinct objects and therefore always false. The 'override is unavailable/unbooked' branch never fires; an override whose start equals its end falls through to the time-window checks and, since slotEndTime is neither before nor equal to the (identical) start and slotStartTime is not after the end, it reaches dateOverrideExist=true and the slot is declared available — the exact opposite of the intended semantics.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime (copy-paste), so `end` always equals `start`. A slot whose end time exceeds workingHour.endTime is only rejected if its *start* minute-count also exceeds endTime; any slot that starts inside working hours but ends past closing passes the check and is offered to bookers, producing bookings outside the host's stated availability.

[BUG] The working-hours check compares slotStartTime.day()/hour()/minute() — computed in UTC — against workingHour.startTime/endTime/days, which are in the organizer's local timezone, with no timezone conversion anywhere in the new block. For any organizer not on UTC, every slot is evaluated against the wrong day-of-week and wrong minute range: a Monday 09:00 organizer slot in UTC+6 is checked as Sunday 03:00 and rejected against working hours, so legitimate slots disappear from the schedule for non-UTC organizers even when they have no date override at all (the working-hours block now runs unconditionally whenever workingHours is non-empty).

[BUG] `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` parses a Date object with the timezone plugin's parsing path as if it were a wall-clock string, discarding the Date's absolute instant. dayjs.tz(Date) reinterprets the stored local-time components (in the server's OS timezone, via the Date's toString) as wall time in organizerTimeZone, so utcOffset is computed from a shifted wall-clock time; around DST transitions or on servers not on UTC, the derived utcOffset is wrong by the server's own offset, and every date-override boundary computed from it (the add(utcOffset, 'minutes') calls) shifts by that error, blocking or exposing the wrong slots.

[BUG] `override.timeZone` is optional in TimeRange (schedule.d.ts adds `timeZone?: string`) but getSlots calls `.tz(override.timeZone)` and `.tz(timeZone)` with no guard, so any caller that builds dateOverrides without the new timeZone field silently falls back to the server's local timezone. Every other producer of dateOverrides that feeds getSlots (any code path not updated in this diff — the field is optional precisely because nothing enforces it) computes organizerUtcOffset from the server's local zone instead of the organizer's; the resulting offset subtraction yields wrong override minute-ranges and working-hours are unset for the wrong window.

[BUG] When dateOverrides is passed but organizerTimeZone is omitted (it is optional), utcOffset is hard-set to 0 rather than the organizer's offset, and the override window is then compared in raw UTC against UTC slot times. Any invocation reaching checkIfIsAvailable with dateOverrides but without organizerTimeZone (both parameters are optional and defaulted, nothing type-level prevents it — e.g. the round-robin/collective branch at line ~576 resolves `userSchedule?.timeZone` which is undefined when the slot's userId doesn't match any userAvailability entry) treats the override as if the organizer were on UTC, marking the wrong calendar day as overridden and zeroing working hours for the wrong date.

[ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable gained optional dateOverrides/workingHours/organizerTimeZone parameters that silently default to empty, making the function's behavior depend on which optional bags the caller remembered to spread. A future caller (or one of the several existing call sites in this file that spreads different props — some spread `...schedule`, others `...availabilityCheckProps`, others `...userSchedule`) that omits workingHours gets slots returned with no working-hours constraint at all, an availability leak that fails silently in production rather than at compile time; a required-props signature or a single options object would make the omission a type error.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose start falls inside working hours but which extends past the working-hours end is never rejected. A 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before workingHours.endTime passes the check (`end` equals `start`, which is < endTime), so getSchedule returns slots that overrun the host's working hours; users book events the host never agreed to host. Note also the whole workingHours branch is only reachable for slots on days without overrides, so every normal (non-override) day's slot validation now depends on this broken comparison.

[BUG] When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside the override window, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true before reaching the `busy` check, so existing bookings and calendar events are ignored. `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` executes unconditionally before the `busy.every(...)` block; any booked time or imported calendar busy event inside a date override is offered as available, enabling double-bookings on override days.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, which is always false. Zero-length date overrides (start === end, intended per the original condition to mean 'unavailable all day') are never detected as such; the intended 'block the entire day' semantics for empty overrides silently never fires, and the code instead falls through to the boundary comparisons.

[BUG] `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` is called with a Date object, which dayjs interprets as the wall-clock time of that Date expressed in organizerTimeZone rather than converting the instant — the resulting utcOffset is derived from a shifted timestamp. For hosts in timezones with DST or nonzero offsets, the computed utcOffset corresponds to a different wall time than the override's actual instant, so the override's day-match (`format("YYYY MM DD")`) misclassifies which calendar day a slot belongs to and slots near midnight get incorrectly included/excluded from override windows.

[BUG] The offset for the whole override is computed once from `override.start` only, and from `override.start.toString()` which is a local-time string reinterpreted in the target zones, so overrides that span a DST transition or are evaluated on a server with a different local timezone get the wrong minute offset. For an override starting the day before a DST change (or any server whose TZ differs from UTC), `dayjs(override.start.toString())` shifts the instant by the server's local offset, so `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` is wrong and the override's start/end minutes of day are off by up to an hour — slots are unhidden or wrongly hidden for that day.

[ADVISORY] The only added test covers the timezone-offset case in packages/lib/slots.ts; none of the substantially new logic in checkIfIsAvailable (working-hours rejection, date-override day gating, busy-check bypass on override days) is exercised by any test in this diff. The `end`-computed-from-start bug in the workingHours check and the busy-bypass on override days ship to production undetected; the diff adds ~70 lines of new availability logic in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts with zero assertions covering it, so the next refactor of getSchedule regresses silently.

[ADVISORY] The new working-hours rejection in checkIfIsAvailable duplicates, with a different implementation, the working-hours logic already applied in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots via `isAvailable` — two parallel sources of truth for 'slot is within working hours' that can drift (and already disagree, since this copy is broken). Maintainers changing availability semantics must now update two code paths in two packages; because they use different data shapes (minutes-of-day vs dayjs comparisons), a fix to one will not propagate to the other, producing inconsistent slot availability between the slot-generation and slot-filtering stages.

[BUG] The new working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable computes `start` and `end` from the same expression (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` for both), so the slot's end is never checked. A slot that starts inside working hours but whose event end falls past workingHour.endTime passes the check because `end` is identical to `start`; `end > workingHour.endTime` only ever rejects slots whose start time exceeds closing time. Users can book meetings that overrun the host's working hours in any multi-step flow where this filter is the deciding check.

[BUG] The zero-length override branch compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality on distinct objects and is always false. Zero-length (unavailable-all-day) date overrides never match this branch, so instead of returning true (unavailable) the code falls through to the time comparisons, where slotEndTime is after override start and slotStartTime is before override end is false — a zero-length override silently makes the whole day available via `dateOverrideExist = true; return true`, the exact opposite of unavailability.

[BUG] The organizer-offset conversion applies the utcOffset with the wrong sign: `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` is added to the UTC instant, moving the local-date computation in the opposite direction of the organizer's timezone. For a +6:00 organizer, utcOffset is +360 and the code subtracts 360 minutes, so the computed override 'day' is the previous UTC-relative local day; slots on the actual override day are treated as outside the override (blocked by the `return false` path) and slots on the neighboring day are wrongly allowed/blocked. This also contradicts the sibling implementation in packages/lib/slots.ts which computes `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` — same concern implemented with opposite sign conventions in the same PR.

[ADVISORY] This PR adds a second, independent implementation of date-override and working-hours filtering inside checkIfIsAvailable, parallel to the existing filtering in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots, and the two have already drifted (opposite offset sign conventions, different override-matching semantics). The next maintainer changing override semantics must find and correctly update both implementations; the sign-convention drift introduced within this very diff demonstrates the failure mode. Either the lib/slots.ts logic or this filter becomes authoritative and the other silently disagrees, producing schedules where slot generation and availability filtering disagree about the same override.

[ADVISORY] The working-hours rejection predicate is inverted relative to its intent: it returns `true` from `find` (leading to `return false`) when `start < workingHour.startTime` — i.e. it rejects slots that start before opening, which is correct — but because `end` equals `start` (see separate finding) the intended 'slot overruns closing time' rule is unreachable, leaving a half-implemented rule shipped. Callers relying on this filter for boundary enforcement get asymmetric protection: early starts blocked, late overruns allowed. Anyone booking at the last minute of a working window gets an event extending past close.

[BUG] The fixed-hosts availability check passes the invitee's schedule timezone as `organizerTimeZone`, a confusable-pair misbinding. `schedule` here is the per-timezone schedule computed from the booking user's `input.timeZone`; passing `schedule.timeZone` as `organizerTimeZone` means date-override wall-date matching in `checkIfIsAvailable` is computed in the invitee's timezone instead of the organizer's, so when the two fall on different calendar dates the slot is wrongly filtered out or wrongly admitted for fixed hosts.

[BUG] The working-hours end computation is a copy-paste bug: `end` is derived from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`. `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` makes `end` identical to `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test never checks the slot's end time — a 60-minute slot starting at 16:50 against a 17:00 working-hours end passes and is offered even though it overruns the host's availability by 50 minutes.

[BUG] The new working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` compares UTC slot times against organizer-local working-hours values with no timezone conversion. `slotStartTime` comes from `time.utc()` while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are stored in the host's local time; a host in +6:00 with working hours 09:00–17:00 local gets slots 09:00–17:00 UTC offered (i.e. 15:00–23:00 local) and vice versa — every non-UTC host gets slots shifted by their offset outside their real working hours, because the `organizerTimeZone` needed for conversion is never applied to this block.

[BUG] The full-day-override equality check compares two dayjs wrapper objects with `===`, which is always false. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` performs reference equality on freshly constructed dayjs instances, so the intended "override covers the entire day" branch is dead code; full-day overrides fall through to the boundary comparisons instead of unconditionally returning true.

[BUG] Slots that fall inside a date override return true before the `busy.every(...)` check, skipping conflict detection entirely. When `dateOverrideExist` is true but the `find` returned undefined, the function returns true without evaluating the busy list — a slot overlapping an existing booking on a host's special-availability day is offered, and the invitee can create a double-booking because the busy check that previously guarded every slot is bypassed inside overrides.

[BUG] Date overrides are matched against every slot without scoping by userId, even though the flattening in `getSchedule` attaches `userId` per host. In collective and round-robin event types with multiple hosts, one host's date override marks the day as overridden for slots belonging to other hosts too; `checkIfIsAvailable` receives the combined `dateOverrides` array but never filters by `slotUserId`, so a single host's day-off override suppresses or forces other hosts' working hours on that day.

[BUG] The UTC-to-wall-time conversion inverts the offset sign: `utcOffset() * -1` is added instead of subtracted. Wall-clock time is instant + utcOffset (offset in minutes east), but the code adds `-utcOffset`; for a +6:00 organizer an override stored as 2024-01-02T00:00 local (UTC 2024-01-01T18:00) is shifted to 2024-01-01T12:00 instead of 2024-01-02T00:00, so the `format("YYYY MM DD")` comparison matches the wrong calendar day and override-day slots are incorrectly filtered for every non-UTC organizer.

[ADVISORY] The override→minutes conversion in `getSlots` and the override-window logic newly added to `checkIfIsAvailable` are two parallel hand-maintained implementations of the same "which slots does a date override cover" rule with different offset arithmetic. One path converts via `utcOffset` deltas between invitee and organizer; the other via `utcOffset * -1` against the organizer. They will drift (the working-hours `end` copy-paste bug already shows the pattern), and the next timezone-related change has to be made correctly in two places or slot generation and slot filtering disagree, silently hiding or resurrecting slots.

[ADVISORY] The DST offset is computed once at `override.start` and applied to both `override.start` and `override.end`. For an override spanning a DST transition (e.g. a 2024-11-03 multi-day or evening-to-morning override in a US timezone), the end time is shifted by the start's offset, misplacing the override boundary by up to an hour; hosts in DST-observing timezones see phantom or missing slots on transition days.

[BUG] Object-identity comparison of two dayjs instances `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is always false, so the intended "zero-length override means unavailable" branch never executes. Zero-length (unavailable-all-day) date overrides never return true from the find callback; the surrounding logic then falls through to the working-hours path, so a user who marked a day fully unavailable sees bookable slots returned in the API response.

[BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`) instead of `slotEndTime`, so the check tests a zero-length interval and never validates whether the slot's end crosses the working-hours boundary. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after working hours endTime is reported as available; invitees can book events that run past the host's stated availability end.

[BUG] The parameter named `organizerTimeZone` is passed `schedule.timeZone`, which is the invitee's/queried schedule timezone (the same value used to render times for the requester), not the organizer's timezone computed at line ~439. Inside checkIfIsAvailable, `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` is computed with the invitee's timezone, so the override date-match is evaluated against the invitee's calendar day instead of the organizer's — the two timezones computed in packages/lib/slots.ts (organizer vs invitee offset math) and this check disagree, producing wrongly filtered slots whenever invitee and organizer are on different dates.

[BUG] When a slot falls on a date that has an override but the find callback returns undefined (slot inside the override window, or the override doesn't fully rule it out), `dateOverrideExist` short-circuits to `return true` without consulting `busy` — the availability check for busy times is entirely skipped for any slot on an overridden date. A slot on an overridden date that collides with an existing booking passes checkIfIsAvailable because the busy check is bypassed; double-bookings become bookable on any day with a date override.

[ADVISORY] The override time math `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + ...minute()` drops the date component and can yield an inverted window when an override crosses midnight in either timezone (e.g. negative or >1440 values), and the subsequent loop that unsets working hours then operates on out-of-range minute values. Hosts whose date overrides cross midnight (e.g. 23:00–01:00) get working hours incorrectly unset for the wrong day; silent wrong availability surfaced to invitees.

[ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable gained date-override and working-hours re-validation logic that duplicates the filtering already performed by getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts — two parallel implementations of "what does an override mean" that can (and per the findings above, do) diverge. The next change to override semantics must be made in two places; the divergence already manifests as slots available in one path and blocked in the other. Should be a single source of truth or the duplicate check deleted.

[ADVISORY] The new date-override and working-hours filtering branches in checkIfIsAvailable are exercised by no test in this diff, so the assertion `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` (a reference comparison that is always false) and the workingHours branch that computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of the working hour's end would both pass the existing suite unnoticed. A regression in these new branches ships silently: slots that fall inside a date override get rejected (or accepted) incorrectly, and any slot outside 09:00–17:00 UTC is excluded because `end` mirrors `start`; the only test added (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts) asserts output of the getSlots override timezone path in packages/lib/slots.ts, never entering these branches. Checked for covering tests in: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts (the only test file in the diff) — its new case only varies the invitee timeZone, which routes through getSlots, not the new checkIfIsAvailable logic.

[ADVISORY] The new test asserts the exact same slot list (08:30Z–11:30Z on plus2DateString) as the test immediately above it for the UTC case, and its comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time' documents that no output change is expected — so the test passes whether or not the timezone-offset fix in packages/lib/slots.ts is correct, and even if the fix were reverted. Future regressions in the offset computation (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` in packages/lib/slots.ts:212-215) for this configuration go undetected because the assertion is identical to the no-offset baseline; a meaningful test would pick a case where old code and new code produce different slots (e.g. an organizer override whose UTC hour boundaries shift the slot window).

[BUG] The new working-hours check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime`, so `end` is the slot's start minute, not its end minute. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after workingHours.endTime passes the filter (end === start < endTime), so slots overrunning the organizer's workday are offered to bookers; the correct comparison needs slotEndTime.

[BUG] The `dateOverrideExist` short-circuit returns true (available) for any slot falling on an override's date without ever consulting the `busy` array. On days with a date override, existing bookings in `busy` are ignored and overlapped slots are shown as available, allowing double bookings; the busy.every(...) check at the end of the function is unreachable for those days.

[BUG] `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is always false, never the underlying instants. The intended zero-length-override early-out never fires; to be a real instant comparison it must use .isSame(); the branch is dead code and the surrounding boundary logic falls through incorrectly.

[ADVISORY] When `organizerTimeZone` is undefined the override-date comparison silently uses `utcOffset = 0` instead of the actual organizer offset, and the `? : 0` ternary gives no signal of the degraded path. Users booking event types where none of eventType.timeZone, schedule.timeZone, or userAvailability[0].timeZone are set get override-day boundaries computed in UTC, mis-marking which slots count as override-day slots; the next maintainer of this code can't tell from a log or error that the fallback happened.

[BUG] The zero-length override check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separately constructed dayjs object instances with reference equality, which is always false. A date override where start equals end is never detected by this branch; the slot falls through to the time-window comparisons, so the special zero-length override handling silently never executes for any user.

[BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) instead of `slotEndTime`, so `start` and `end` are identical. The `end > workingHour.endTime` guard only ever tests the slot's start minute, so a slot that starts inside working hours but extends past `workingHour.endTime` (e.g., a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before closing) passes the check and is offered to the invitee as bookable despite ending outside working hours.

[BUG] `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` reads a `timeZone` property off `schedule`, which is a `Schedule` (i.e. `TimeRange[][]`), a type that has no `timeZone` member — the value is always `undefined`, even though a correctly computed `organizerTimeZone` variable exists at line ~439 and is not reused here. Inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `organizerTimeZone` is undefined so `utcOffset` falls back to 0 and date-override dates are matched in raw UTC; for any non-UTC organizer the wrong set of slots is marked as in/out of the override window, showing incorrect availability with no error surfaced.

[BUG] `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule.timeZone` and (line ~581) `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` read `timeZone` off a `userSchedule` obtained from `getSchedule(...)`/`userAvailability.find(...)`, whose type (`Schedule` / the availability object's schedule field) has no `timeZone` property, so both always pass `undefined`. The loose-host and round-robin availability checks run date-override date matching with `utcOffset = 0`, silently evaluating the wrong date window for every non-UTC host and returning availability slots that the override should have removed (or vice versa), with no error or signal.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` calls `.tz()` with `override.timeZone`, which the `TimeRange` type declares as optional and is only populated by the `getSchedule` call site in this diff — any other caller of `getSlots` passing date overrides without a `timeZone` gets dayjs's default (server-local) timezone. The organizer UTC offset is computed against the server's local timezone instead of the organizer's, so the shift applied to override start/end times is wrong for any deployment whose server timezone differs from the organizer's, silently producing slot windows at the wrong times.

Therefore the described defect mechanism is not verifiable from this diff.

The diff shows no guard/default when `override.timeZone` is missing, so callers that pass dateOverrides without `timeZone` can yield offsets computed in an unintended timezone (whatever dayjs defaults to), which would shift the computed `startTime`/`endTime` minutes and thus unset working hours for the wrong window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When dateOverrides is passed but organizerTimeZone is omitted (it is optional), utcOffset is hard-set to 0 rather than the organizer's offset, and the override window is then compared in raw UTC against UTC slot times. Any invocation reaching checkIfIsAvailable with dateOverrides but without organizerTimeZone (both parameters are optional and defaulted, nothing type-level prevents it — e.g. the round-robin/collective branch at line ~576 resolves `userSchedule?.timeZone` which is undefined when the slot's userId doesn't match any userAvailability entry) treats the override as if the organizer were on UTC, marking the wrong calendar day as overridden and zeroing working hours for the wrong date.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, dateOverride evaluation depends on `organizerTimeZone`, but when it’s omitted the code forces `utcOffset` to `0` (`organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0`) and then compares shifted `date.start/end` against UTC slot times. Because `dateOverrides` is passed via `...availabilityCheckProps` in multiple call sites, and at least one call passes `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` (which can be `undefined`), this can mis-evaluate overrides as if the organizer were in UTC, potentially applying an override to the wrong calendar day and returning incorrect availability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable gained optional dateOverrides/workingHours/organizerTimeZone parameters that silently default to empty, making the function's behavior depend on which optional bags the caller remembered to spread. A future caller (or one of the several existing call sites in this file that spreads different props — some spread `...schedule`, others `...availabilityCheckProps`, others `...userSchedule`) that omits workingHours gets slots returned with no working-hours constraint at all, an availability leak that fails silently in production rather than at compile time; a required-props signature or a single options object would make the omission a type error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `checkIfIsAvailable` now takes `dateOverrides = []`, `workingHours = []`, and `organizerTimeZone` as optional props (with defaults) in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`. That makes it possible to call the function without providing `workingHours`/`dateOverrides`, and the logic will then skip the “outside working hours” / “date override” constraints and still return availability based only on `busy`. In this PR’s shown call sites, `...availabilityCheckProps` is consistently spread (so the leak doesn’t manifest here), but the API change does create a diff-grounded type-safety/maintenance risk exactly as described: omission would be silent rather than a compile-time error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so a slot whose start falls inside working hours but which extends past the working-hours end is never rejected. A 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before workingHours.endTime passes the check (`end` equals `start`, which is < endTime), so getSchedule returns slots that overrun the host's working hours; users book events the host never agreed to host. Note also the whole workingHours branch is only reachable for slots on days without overrides, so every normal (non-override) day's slot validation now depends on this broken comparison.

[BUG] When a slot falls on a date-override day and inside the override window, `checkIfIsAvailable` returns true before reaching the `busy` check, so existing bookings and calendar events are ignored. `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` executes unconditionally before the `busy.every(...)` block; any booked time or imported calendar busy event inside a date override is offered as available, enabling double-bookings on override days.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the newly added date-override logic returns early: after detecting an override on the slot’s day (`dateOverrideExist = true`), it executes `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` **before** the final `return busy.every(...)` block. That means any slot on an override day that is considered “within” the override window bypasses the busy/calendar conflict check, potentially offering already-booked/busy times as available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares object references, which is always false. Zero-length date overrides (start === end, intended per the original condition to mean 'unavailable all day') are never detected as such; the intended 'block the entire day' semantics for empty overrides silently never fires, and the code instead falls through to the boundary comparisons.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the condition `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two newly-created Dayjs objects by reference, so it will never be true. This makes the intended special-case for zero-length overrides unreachable, and the logic will instead fall through to the boundary checks, changing availability behavior for overrides where start and end represent the same instant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone)` is called with a Date object, which dayjs interprets as the wall-clock time of that Date expressed in organizerTimeZone rather than converting the instant — the resulting utcOffset is derived from a shifted timestamp. For hosts in timezones with DST or nonzero offsets, the computed utcOffset corresponds to a different wall time than the override's actual instant, so the override's day-match (`format("YYYY MM DD")`) misclassifies which calendar day a slot belongs to and slots near midnight get incorrectly included/excluded from override windows.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `utcOffset` is computed via `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`. With Dayjs timezone, passing a `Date` generally represents an absolute instant (ms since epoch) which is then *converted* to the target timezone (equivalent to `dayjs(date.start).tz(organizerTimeZone)`), not re-interpreted as a wall-clock time in that timezone. So the finding’s claim that `Date` is treated as “wall-clock expressed in organizerTimeZone” and therefore produces an offset from a shifted timestamp is not verifiable from the diff and is likely incorrect. (There may still be other issues in this override logic, but not the specific `Date`-interpretation bug described.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The offset for the whole override is computed once from `override.start` only, and from `override.start.toString()` which is a local-time string reinterpreted in the target zones, so overrides that span a DST transition or are evaluated on a server with a different local timezone get the wrong minute offset. For an override starting the day before a DST change (or any server whose TZ differs from UTC), `dayjs(override.start.toString())` shifts the instant by the server's local offset, so `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` is wrong and the override's start/end minutes of day are off by up to an hour — slots are unhidden or wrongly hidden for that day.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the override minute-of-day adjustment computes a single `offset` from `override.start` only (`organizerUtcOffset`/`inviteeUtcOffset`), then applies that same offset to both `override.start` and `override.end` when deriving `startTime`/`endTime`. If either the organizer or invitee timezone crosses a DST boundary between `override.start` and `override.end`, the UTC offset at the end can differ, so using a single offset will produce incorrect end minutes (and potentially start minutes if the override is evaluated on a different day/zone). Additionally, using `dayjs(override.start.toString())` is brittle because it relies on parsing a locale-dependent string representation rather than the `Date` object directly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only added test covers the timezone-offset case in packages/lib/slots.ts; none of the substantially new logic in checkIfIsAvailable (working-hours rejection, date-override day gating, busy-check bypass on override days) is exercised by any test in this diff. The `end`-computed-from-start bug in the workingHours check and the busy-bypass on override days ship to production undetected; the diff adds ~70 lines of new availability logic in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts with zero assertions covering it, so the next refactor of getSchedule regresses silently.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a concrete correctness defect in `checkIfIsAvailable`’s new working-hours gate: it computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so the end-of-slot is never considered and the “outside of working hours” rejection can be wrong. Also, on days where a matching date override exists (`dateOverrideExist`), the function returns `true` before the `busy.every(...)` check, meaning busy times are bypassed on override days. These are real behavioral bugs introduced in the newly added ~70 lines of logic; the added test only targets timezone offset behavior elsewhere and doesn’t cover this logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new working-hours rejection in checkIfIsAvailable duplicates, with a different implementation, the working-hours logic already applied in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots via `isAvailable` — two parallel sources of truth for 'slot is within working hours' that can drift (and already disagree, since this copy is broken). Maintainers changing availability semantics must now update two code paths in two packages; because they use different data shapes (minutes-of-day vs dayjs comparisons), a fix to one will not propagate to the other, producing inconsistent slot availability between the slot-generation and slot-filtering stages.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a second, independent working-hours gate inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts) even though working-hours are already modeled/applied earlier in slot computation (e.g., packages/lib/slots.ts `getSlots` manipulates availability based on overrides/working hours). This new copy is also visibly incorrect: it computes `const start = ...; const end = ...;` using the same expression (so `end` is not the slot end and ignores `eventLength`/`slotEndTime`), meaning slots that overrun `workingHour.endTime` won’t be rejected, and the semantics can diverge from the minutes-of-day logic in `getSlots`. This can produce inconsistent availability between slot generation and filtering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable computes `start` and `end` from the same expression (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` for both), so the slot's end is never checked. A slot that starts inside working hours but whose event end falls past workingHour.endTime passes the check because `end` is identical to `start`; `end > workingHour.endTime` only ever rejects slots whose start time exceeds closing time. Users can book meetings that overrun the host's working hours in any multi-step flow where this filter is the deciding check.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours guard computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime` (`const start = ...; const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`). This makes `end` identical to `start`, so the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` never checks the slot’s true end (which should be based on `slotEndTime`). As a result, a slot can start within working hours but extend past `workingHour.endTime` without being rejected by this check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zero-length override branch compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is reference equality on distinct objects and is always false. Zero-length (unavailable-all-day) date overrides never match this branch, so instead of returning true (unavailable) the code falls through to the time comparisons, where slotEndTime is after override start and slotStartTime is before override end is false — a zero-length override silently makes the whole day available via `dateOverrideExist = true; return true`, the exact opposite of unavailability.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the “zero-length override” check uses `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )` (reference equality). These are distinct Dayjs instances, so this condition is effectively never true even when the timestamps are equal. As a result, the special handling for `start === end` overrides is skipped and the function can fall through to `dateOverrideExist` logic (`if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`), incorrectly marking some slots as available when the override was intended to block availability for that day/time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer-offset conversion applies the utcOffset with the wrong sign: `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` is added to the UTC instant, moving the local-date computation in the opposite direction of the organizer's timezone. For a +6:00 organizer, utcOffset is +360 and the code subtracts 360 minutes, so the computed override 'day' is the previous UTC-relative local day; slots on the actual override day are treated as outside the override (blocked by the `return false` path) and slots on the neighboring day are wrongly allowed/blocked. This also contradicts the sibling implementation in packages/lib/slots.ts which computes `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` — same concern implemented with opposite sign conventions in the same PR.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the code derives `utcOffset` as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then does `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` for day-comparisons against `slotStartTime` (which is forced to UTC). For a positive-offset organizer timezone (e.g. +6:00 => `utcOffset()` = +360), multiplying by `-1` and adding -360 minutes shifts the instant backwards, changing the computed YYYY-MM-DD in the opposite direction of the organizer’s local time. This can misclassify which UTC day corresponds to the organizer’s override day. The same PR’s logic in `packages/lib/slots.ts` computes an offset as `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` (without this sign inversion), highlighting an inconsistent/sign-mismatched convention across the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This PR adds a second, independent implementation of date-override and working-hours filtering inside checkIfIsAvailable, parallel to the existing filtering in packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots, and the two have already drifted (opposite offset sign conventions, different override-matching semantics). The next maintainer changing override semantics must find and correctly update both implementations; the sign-convention drift introduced within this very diff demonstrates the failure mode. Either the lib/slots.ts logic or this filter becomes authoritative and the other silently disagrees, producing schedules where slot generation and availability filtering disagree about the same override.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate pieces of logic now handling date overrides/timezone-adjustment and working-hours constraints: (1) `packages/lib/slots.ts` `getSlots` applies `activeOverrides` by computing an `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and shifting override start/end by `add(offset, "minute")`; (2) `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` `checkIfIsAvailable` newly adds its own date-override gating and working-hours gating (using `dateOverrides`/`workingHours`) and computes a timezone adjustment as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`. This is indeed an independent implementation parallel to `getSlots`, and the offset handling differs in sign/convention and semantics (e.g., `checkIfIsAvailable` returns `true` immediately when any override exists for the day, bypassing working-hours checks, while `getSlots` mutates working hours based on overrides). That duplication/drift is a concrete maintainability/consistency risk grounded in the diff, even if it may be intentional and not provably a user-visible defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The working-hours rejection predicate is inverted relative to its intent: it returns `true` from `find` (leading to `return false`) when `start < workingHour.startTime` — i.e. it rejects slots that start before opening, which is correct — but because `end` equals `start` (see separate finding) the intended 'slot overruns closing time' rule is unreachable, leaving a half-implemented rule shipped. Callers relying on this filter for boundary enforcement get asymmetric protection: early starts blocked, late overruns allowed. Anyone booking at the last minute of a working window gets an event extending past close.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the new working-hours gate computes `start` and `end` identically from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), then rejects when `end > workingHour.endTime`. Because `end` never reflects the slot’s end (nor `slotEndTime`/`eventLength`), a slot that starts within working hours but extends past `workingHour.endTime` will not be rejected. This is a real correctness bug introduced by the diff’s new working-hours enforcement logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fixed-hosts availability check passes the invitee's schedule timezone as `organizerTimeZone`, a confusable-pair misbinding. `schedule` here is the per-timezone schedule computed from the booking user's `input.timeZone`; passing `schedule.timeZone` as `organizerTimeZone` means date-override wall-date matching in `checkIfIsAvailable` is computed in the invitee's timezone instead of the organizer's, so when the two fall on different calendar dates the slot is wrongly filtered out or wrongly admitted for fixed hosts.

adjudication.rationale: In `getSchedule`, a stable `organizerTimeZone` is computed from `eventType.timeZone || eventType?.schedule?.timeZone || userAvailability?.[0]?.timeZone` and passed into `getTimeSlots`, but when later calling `checkIfIsAvailable` for the main slot-availability pass, the code passes `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` instead (`organizerTimeZone` is not used there). `checkIfIsAvailable` uses `organizerTimeZone` to compute a UTC offset for date-override day matching (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`), so feeding it the schedule's timezone (which is derived from the schedule being evaluated, not necessarily the organizer's) can shift the wall-date comparison and incorrectly admit/filter slots when invitee/organizer dates differ.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours end computation is a copy-paste bug: `end` is derived from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`. `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` makes `end` identical to `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` test never checks the slot's end time — a 60-minute slot starting at 16:50 against a 17:00 working-hours end passes and is offered even though it overruns the host's availability by 50 minutes.

[BUG] The new working-hours check in `checkIfIsAvailable` compares UTC slot times against organizer-local working-hours values with no timezone conversion. `slotStartTime` comes from `time.utc()` while `workingHour.startTime/endTime` are stored in the host's local time; a host in +6:00 with working hours 09:00–17:00 local gets slots 09:00–17:00 UTC offered (i.e. 15:00–23:00 local) and vice versa — every non-UTC host gets slots shifted by their offset outside their real working hours, because the `organizerTimeZone` needed for conversion is never applied to this block.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours block computes `start`/`end` from `slotStartTime`, where `slotStartTime` is explicitly `time.utc()` (UTC day/hour/minute). It then compares those UTC-derived minutes against `workingHour.startTime/endTime` with no conversion using `organizerTimeZone` (which is only used in the date-override logic). If `workingHours` are expressed in the organizer’s local time (as is typical for schedule working hours), this will shift availability for non-UTC organizers. The diff shows no timezone normalization applied in this block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The full-day-override equality check compares two dayjs wrapper objects with `===`, which is always false. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` performs reference equality on freshly constructed dayjs instances, so the intended "override covers the entire day" branch is dead code; full-day overrides fall through to the boundary comparisons instead of unconditionally returning true.

[BUG] Slots that fall inside a date override return true before the `busy.every(...)` check, skipping conflict detection entirely. When `dateOverrideExist` is true but the `find` returned undefined, the function returns true without evaluating the busy list — a slot overlapping an existing booking on a host's special-availability day is offered, and the invitee can create a double-booking because the busy check that previously guarded every slot is bypassed inside overrides.

adjudication.rationale:
In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the new date-override logic runs, the function does:

- `if (dateOverrides.find(...)) { return false; }` (meaning the slot is outside the override window for that day)
- then `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`

That `return true` occurs before the final `return busy.every((busyTime) => { ... })` conflict check, so any slot that is within a date override day/window bypasses `busy` conflict detection entirely. This matches the finding: on a special-availability day, a slot overlapping an existing booking could be treated as available because the busy check is skipped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Date overrides are matched against every slot without scoping by userId, even though the flattening in `getSchedule` attaches `userId` per host. In collective and round-robin event types with multiple hosts, one host's date override marks the day as overridden for slots belonging to other hosts too; `checkIfIsAvailable` receives the combined `dateOverrides` array but never filters by `slotUserId`, so a single host's day-off override suppresses or forces other hosts' working hours on that day.

adjudication.rationale: In `getSchedule`, `dateOverrides` are flattened across all hosts and now include `{ userId, timeZone, ...override }` (see mapping around `availability.dateOverrides.map(...)`). However, `checkIfIsAvailable` accepts `dateOverrides?: { start: Date; end: Date; }[]` (no `userId`) and its logic checks `dateOverrides.find(...)` without filtering by the slot’s host/user. In collective/round-robin flows, `checkIfIsAvailable` is invoked per-slot (and sometimes per-user) but still receives the combined `dateOverrides` array via `availabilityCheckProps`, so one host’s override can affect availability checks for other hosts’ slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The UTC-to-wall-time conversion inverts the offset sign: `utcOffset() * -1` is added instead of subtracted. Wall-clock time is instant + utcOffset (offset in minutes east), but the code adds `-utcOffset`; for a +6:00 organizer an override stored as 2024-01-02T00:00 local (UTC 2024-01-01T18:00) is shifted to 2024-01-01T12:00 instead of 2024-01-02T00:00, so the `format("YYYY MM DD")` comparison matches the wrong calendar day and override-day slots are incorrectly filtered for every non-UTC organizer.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the code computes `utcOffset = dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then does `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` for day and boundary comparisons. Since `utcOffset()` is minutes east of UTC, converting an instant to organizer wall time requires adding the (positive) offset, not adding the negated offset. As written, for a +06:00 organizer it shifts the override earlier by 6h (e.g., 18:00Z -> 12:00Z) which can change the `YYYY MM DD` and cause overrides to be matched/filtered on the wrong day for non-UTC organizers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The override→minutes conversion in `getSlots` and the override-window logic newly added to `checkIfIsAvailable` are two parallel hand-maintained implementations of the same "which slots does a date override cover" rule with different offset arithmetic. One path converts via `utcOffset` deltas between invitee and organizer; the other via `utcOffset * -1` against the organizer. They will drift (the working-hours `end` copy-paste bug already shows the pattern), and the next timezone-related change has to be made correctly in two places or slot generation and slot filtering disagree, silently hiding or resurrecting slots.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce two separate, hand-maintained pieces of logic for interpreting date overrides against slots. In `packages/lib/slots.ts#getSlots`, overrides are converted into minute ranges by computing an offset delta between `override.timeZone` (organizer) and the `timeZone` argument (invitee) via `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, then shifting `override.start/end` by that delta before extracting hour/minute. Separately, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts#checkIfIsAvailable` adds new date-override window checks that adjust using `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and compares against `slotStartTime/slotEndTime` without incorporating any invitee-vs-organizer delta. These are parallel implementations of “which times does an override cover” with different offset arithmetic, so they can diverge and cause slot generation (`getSlots`) and slot filtering (`checkIfIsAvailable`) to disagree. This is a concrete maintainability/consistency issue grounded in the diff, even if the diff alone can’t prove a specific failing scenario today.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The DST offset is computed once at `override.start` and applied to both `override.start` and `override.end`. For an override spanning a DST transition (e.g. a 2024-11-03 multi-day or evening-to-morning override in a US timezone), the end time is shifted by the start's offset, misplacing the override boundary by up to an hour; hosts in DST-observing timezones see phantom or missing slots on transition days.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the override adjustment computes `organizerUtcOffset` and `inviteeUtcOffset` only from `override.start` and derives a single `offset` (invitee - organizer). That same `offset` is then applied to both `override.start` and `override.end` (`dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute")...`). If the override spans a DST transition, the UTC offset at `override.end` can differ from `override.start` in either timezone, so applying the start-derived offset to the end will shift the override boundary by up to an hour, producing incorrect slot inclusion/exclusion on transition days.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Object-identity comparison of two dayjs instances `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` is always false, so the intended "zero-length override means unavailable" branch never executes. Zero-length (unavailable-all-day) date overrides never return true from the find callback; the surrounding logic then falls through to the working-hours path, so a user who marked a day fully unavailable sees bookable slots returned in the API response.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the code compares two newly-created Dayjs objects by identity: `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )`. This will never be true unless they are the exact same object, so the intended zero-length override check cannot trigger. Because `dateOverrideExist` is set to true for matching dates, but the `.find(...)` callback returns no truthy value for many slots when `start === end`, the surrounding `if (dateOverrides.find(...)) { return false; }` is skipped and the function then hits `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`, incorrectly marking slots available when a zero-length override should block them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`) instead of `slotEndTime`, so the check tests a zero-length interval and never validates whether the slot's end crosses the working-hours boundary. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after working hours endTime is reported as available; invitees can book events that run past the host's stated availability end.

[BUG] The parameter named `organizerTimeZone` is passed `schedule.timeZone`, which is the invitee's/queried schedule timezone (the same value used to render times for the requester), not the organizer's timezone computed at line ~439. Inside checkIfIsAvailable, `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` is computed with the invitee's timezone, so the override date-match is evaluated against the invitee's calendar day instead of the organizer's — the two timezones computed in packages/lib/slots.ts (organizer vs invitee offset math) and this check disagree, producing wrongly filtered slots whenever invitee and organizer are on different dates.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `checkIfIsAvailable` being called with `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` (and `userSchedule.timeZone` elsewhere) rather than the earlier computed `organizerTimeZone` variable. However, the finding’s core claim—that `schedule.timeZone` is the invitee/requester timezone used for rendering—is not verifiable from this diff; `schedule.timeZone` plausibly refers to the organizer/user schedule timezone (especially since `dateOverrides` now carry `timeZone: availability.timeZone`). Without seeing what `schedule` represents, we cannot confirm the alleged organizer/invitee timezone mix-up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When a slot falls on a date that has an override but the find callback returns undefined (slot inside the override window, or the override doesn't fully rule it out), `dateOverrideExist` short-circuits to `return true` without consulting `busy` — the availability check for busy times is entirely skipped for any slot on an overridden date. A slot on an overridden date that collides with an existing booking passes checkIfIsAvailable because the busy check is bypassed; double-bookings become bookable on any day with a date override.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, when a slot’s date matches a `dateOverrides` entry, the code sets `dateOverrideExist = true` inside the `.find` callback. If the slot is *within* the override window, the callback returns `undefined`, so the outer `if (dateOverrides.find(...)) { return false; }` does not trigger. Immediately after, `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` returns early, skipping the final `busy.every(...)` collision check. Therefore, any slot on an overridden day that falls inside the override window can be marked available even if it overlaps an existing busy interval, enabling double-booking on override days.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The override time math `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + ...minute()` drops the date component and can yield an inverted window when an override crosses midnight in either timezone (e.g. negative or >1440 values), and the subsequent loop that unsets working hours then operates on out-of-range minute values. Hosts whose date overrides cross midnight (e.g. 23:00–01:00) get working hours incorrectly unset for the wrong day; silent wrong availability surfaced to invitees.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as minutes-of-day via `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour()*60 + ...minute()`, which discards the date component. If an override window crosses midnight after applying the organizer↔invitee offset, this representation can produce an inverted range (e.g., startTime > endTime) with no handling for wraparound, and the later logic that “unsets all working hours that relate to this user availability override” will act on the wrong portion of the day. The finding’s mention of negative or >1440 values isn’t shown (hour/minute keep it 0–1439), but the core midnight-crossing/inversion risk is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable gained date-override and working-hours re-validation logic that duplicates the filtering already performed by getSlots in packages/lib/slots.ts — two parallel implementations of "what does an override mean" that can (and per the findings above, do) diverge. The next change to override semantics must be made in two places; the divergence already manifests as slots available in one path and blocked in the other. Should be a single source of truth or the duplicate check deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate implementations of date-override/working-hours semantics: (1) `packages/lib/slots.ts#getSlots` mutates/unsets working hours based on `activeOverrides` (now with timezone offset math), and (2) `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts#checkIfIsAvailable` newly re-checks `dateOverrides` and `workingHours` to accept/reject a slot. This is a concrete, diff-grounded duplication that can easily diverge because override meaning must be maintained in both places. However, the claim that divergence already manifests as contradictory availability is not directly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new date-override and working-hours filtering branches in checkIfIsAvailable are exercised by no test in this diff, so the assertion `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` (a reference comparison that is always false) and the workingHours branch that computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of the working hour's end would both pass the existing suite unnoticed. A regression in these new branches ships silently: slots that fall inside a date override get rejected (or accepted) incorrectly, and any slot outside 09:00–17:00 UTC is excluded because `end` mirrors `start`; the only test added (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts) asserts output of the getSlots override timezone path in packages/lib/slots.ts, never entering these branches. Checked for covering tests in: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts (the only test file in the diff) — its new case only varies the invitee timeZone, which routes through getSlots, not the new checkIfIsAvailable logic.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the new date-override logic contains a real correctness defect: `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so it will effectively never be true (it should likely use `.isSame(...)`). Also, the new working-hours check computes `end` from `slotStartTime` again (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so `end` always equals `start`, which breaks the intended “slot must fit within workingHour.startTime/endTime” logic (it won’t properly account for slot duration / end time). These are verifiable from the diff and can cause incorrect accept/reject decisions for slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new test asserts the exact same slot list (08:30Z–11:30Z on plus2DateString) as the test immediately above it for the UTC case, and its comment 'it should return the same as this is the utc time' documents that no output change is expected — so the test passes whether or not the timezone-offset fix in packages/lib/slots.ts is correct, and even if the fix were reverted. Future regressions in the offset computation (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` in packages/lib/slots.ts:212-215) for this configuration go undetected because the assertion is identical to the no-offset baseline; a meaningful test would pick a case where old code and new code produce different slots (e.g. an organizer override whose UTC hour boundaries shift the slot window).

adjudication.rationale: The added test in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` calls `getSchedule` with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` but asserts the exact same slot list (`["08:30:00.000Z", "09:30:00.000Z", "10:30:00.000Z", "11:30:00.000Z"]` on `plus2DateString`) as the preceding UTC-oriented expectation, and the inline comment explicitly states “it should return the same”. From the diff alone, this makes it likely the test does not distinguish between the pre-change override handling (previously based on `getUTCHours()/getUTCMinutes()`) and the new offset computation in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`), so it may not actually detect regressions in that new logic for this scenario. This is a specific, diff-grounded test-coverage weakness rather than a functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new working-hours check computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime`, so `end` is the slot's start minute, not its end minute. A slot that starts within working hours but ends after workingHours.endTime passes the filter (end === start < endTime), so slots overrunning the organizer's workday are offered to bookers; the correct comparison needs slotEndTime.

[BUG] The `dateOverrideExist` short-circuit returns true (available) for any slot falling on an override's date without ever consulting the `busy` array. On days with a date override, existing bookings in `busy` are ignored and overlapped slots are shown as available, allowing double bookings; the busy.every(...) check at the end of the function is unreachable for those days.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override logic can return availability before consulting `busy`: after the `dateOverrides.find(...)` block, if any override exists on the slot’s date (`dateOverrideExist` set true) and the slot is *not* outside the override window (so the `.find` does not trigger the early `return false`), the function immediately `return true;` (lines added around `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`). This bypasses the subsequent `return busy.every(...)` conflict check, so on days with a matching date override, overlapping `busy` intervals can be ignored and double-bookable slots can be shown as available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes"))` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, which is always false, never the underlying instants. The intended zero-length-override early-out never fires; to be a real instant comparison it must use .isSame(); the branch is dead code and the surrounding boundary logic falls through incorrectly.
matched_golden_ids: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using `===` compares Dayjs object references rather than their underlying time values, making the condition always false, and recommends using `.isSame()` for a real instant comparison—exactly the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When `organizerTimeZone` is undefined the override-date comparison silently uses `utcOffset = 0` instead of the actual organizer offset, and the `? : 0` ternary gives no signal of the degraded path. Users booking event types where none of eventType.timeZone, schedule.timeZone, or userAvailability[0].timeZone are set get override-day boundaries computed in UTC, mis-marking which slots count as override-day slots; the next maintainer of this code can't tell from a log or error that the fallback happened.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, override-day matching depends on `organizerTimeZone`, but when it is falsy it explicitly falls back to `utcOffset = 0` (`const utcOffset = organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0;`). This is a silent degraded path (no log/error) and changes semantics: override-day boundaries are treated as UTC when the organizer TZ isn’t provided. The finding’s exact source list (eventType.timeZone/schedule.timeZone/userAvailability[0].timeZone) isn’t what is directly used here (calls pass `schedule.timeZone`/`userSchedule?.timeZone`), but `organizerTimeZone` can still be `undefined` (e.g., `userSchedule?.timeZone`), making the silent UTC fallback a real, diff-grounded maintainability/edge-case concern rather than a provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zero-length override check `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separately constructed dayjs object instances with reference equality, which is always false. A date override where start equals end is never detected by this branch; the slot falls through to the time-window comparisons, so the special zero-length override handling silently never executes for any user.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new zero-length override branch uses `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )`. These are two separately constructed Dayjs objects, so `===` compares references and will essentially never be true. As a result, the intended special handling for overrides where `start` equals `end` will never execute, and the slot will fall through to the later logic (including `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;`), changing availability behavior for that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`) instead of `slotEndTime`, so `start` and `end` are identical. The `end > workingHour.endTime` guard only ever tests the slot's start minute, so a slot that starts inside working hours but extends past `workingHour.endTime` (e.g., a 60-minute slot starting 30 minutes before closing) passes the check and is offered to the invitee as bookable despite ending outside working hours.

[BUG] `organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` reads a `timeZone` property off `schedule`, which is a `Schedule` (i.e. `TimeRange[][]`), a type that has no `timeZone` member — the value is always `undefined`, even though a correctly computed `organizerTimeZone` variable exists at line ~439 and is not reused here. Inside `checkIfIsAvailable`, `organizerTimeZone` is undefined so `utcOffset` falls back to 0 and date-override dates are matched in raw UTC; for any non-UTC organizer the wrong set of slots is marked as in/out of the override window, showing incorrect availability with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on `schedule` being a `Schedule` (`TimeRange[][]`) and therefore lacking a `timeZone` member, making `schedule.timeZone` “always undefined”. From the diff alone, the type of the local variable named `schedule` in `getSchedule` is not shown/derivable, and it is already being object-spread (`...schedule`), which strongly suggests it’s an object (e.g., a per-user schedule/busy bundle) rather than a raw `TimeRange[][]` array. Additionally, the diff adds `timeZone?: string` to `TimeRange`, indicating timezone is expected on range-like objects, undermining the claim that accessing `.timeZone` is necessarily invalid here. So the asserted definite bug (“always undefined”) cannot be verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule.timeZone` and (line ~581) `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` read `timeZone` off a `userSchedule` obtained from `getSchedule(...)`/`userAvailability.find(...)`, whose type (`Schedule` / the availability object's schedule field) has no `timeZone` property, so both always pass `undefined`. The loose-host and round-robin availability checks run date-override date matching with `utcOffset = 0`, silently evaluating the wrong date window for every non-UTC host and returning availability slots that the override should have removed (or vice versa), with no error or signal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `userSchedule` is obtained via `userAvailability.find(...)` (not from the `Schedule`/`availability.schedule` field), and the same file already reads `availability.timeZone` when constructing `dateOverrides` (`timeZone: availability.timeZone`). That indicates `userAvailability` items do have a `timeZone` property, so `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` is not “always undefined” per the diff. The finding’s claim that the type lacks `timeZone` conflates the `Schedule` type (`TimeRange[][]`) with the `userAvailability` objects being accessed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` calls `.tz()` with `override.timeZone`, which the `TimeRange` type declares as optional and is only populated by the `getSchedule` call site in this diff — any other caller of `getSlots` passing date overrides without a `timeZone` gets dayjs's default (server-local) timezone. The organizer UTC offset is computed against the server's local timezone instead of the organizer's, so the shift applied to override start/end times is wrong for any deployment whose server timezone differs from the organizer's, silently producing slot windows at the wrong times.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic unconditionally does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`. But `TimeRange` now declares `timeZone?: string` (optional) in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`, and `getSlots` does not defensively handle `override.timeZone` being `undefined`. That means callers providing date overrides without `timeZone` can cause `.tz(undefined)` to fall back to an unintended timezone or error, producing incorrect offset calculations (and thus wrong shifted override start/end minutes) compared to the organizer’s intended timezone.
